newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's electricity company's sales up 3.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's electricity company's sales up 3.7 pct.

text.p: Morocco's state-run electricity company's turnover increased by 3.7 percent, reaching 9 billion dirhams ($1.1 billion), in 1996 but there was no comparative figure for the previous year, Morocco's news agency MAP said on Wednesday.

Driss Benhima, Director General of the National Electricity Office (ONE) told a board meeting on Tuesday that the increase was the result of better management and good rains which lifted output of hydroelectric energy.
The higher rainfall had enabled the company to produce nearly 18 percent of national output through hydroelectric plants, compared with only three percent the year before.
Investments for 1996 totalled 4.8 billion dirhams and helped connect 557 villages to the grid.
Benhima said the utility needed to invest 20 billion dirhams ($2.27 billion) to meet demand expected to rise by 6 percent in 1998-2000.
He said 40 percent of the money would be provided by ONE without saying where the rest of the money would be raised.
